answer: Fixed-pool dilution stops bulk fake identities. Each identity claims a wharf berth and files a signed fable, a record of real work, into the crystal ledger; a copied fable burns its bond. Each claim locks 70 credits and pays 35. The pool is fixed at 40,000 and split equally, so each fake dilutes every share. With 200 honest identities, 1,000 fakes pay 35,000, lock 70,000, yet take 33,333, a loss. An honest agent files once for 35, keeps the bond.
